rationale: In the index Sleyp et al. (2022) cohort delineating KLHL20-related neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621390), global developmental delay / intellectual disability was present in 100% of assessed individuals (14/14), whereas seizures (including febrile seizures and epilepsy) showed incomplete penetrance, affecting fewer than 80% (<11/14) of the cohort. Subsequent single-patient reports such as Kuroda et al. (2024) expand the epileptic spectrum to include early-onset West syndrome, but corroborate that developmental delay is the defining, fully penetrant hallmark while epilepsy is incompletely penetrant.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. (2022) reported on 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, finding that all 14 patients had mild to severe intellectual disability/developmental delay, whereas febrile seizures or epilepsy were variable and showed incomplete penetrance.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features.

evidence.text: Kuroda et al. (2024) summarized the existing literature of 14 patients from Sleyp et al. (2022) all exhibiting developmental delay, and reported an additional patient presenting with early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay.

source.title: Early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay associated with a novel KLHL20 variant
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: Fourteen patients have been reported with recurrent missense KLHL20 variants, demonstrating developmental delay

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact sub-phenotypic electroclinical features and long-term seizure outcomes across all reported KLHL20 variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: As newer cases such as West syndrome are documented, systematically cataloging EEG patterns, seizure types, drug-responsiveness, and age-of-onset will determine whether distinct KLHL20 variants drive specific epilepsy syndromes.
